([[Leetsdale, Pennsylvania]]) | college = * [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] (2022–2024) * [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] (2024–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 36 | draft_team = [[Brooklyn Nets]] | career_start = 2025 | years1 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team1 = [[Los Angeles Lakers]] | years2 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team2 = →[[South Bay Lakers]] | highlights = }} '''Adou Thiero''' (born May 8, 2004) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]] and the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]]. ==Early life and high school career== Thiero was born on May 8, 2004 in [[Salt Lake City]], Utah.{{Cite web|url=https://www.proballers.com/basketball/player/257960/adou-thiero|website=Proballers.com|title=Adou Thiero}}{{Cite web |date=May 22, 2024 |title=Adou Thiero |url=https://arkansasrazorbacks.com/roster/adou-thiero/ |access-date=January 17, 2025 |website=Arkansas Razorbacks |language=en-US}} His parents, Almamy and Mariam, immigrated to the U.S. from [[Mali]] and both played [[college basketball]]; his father Almamy for [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] under coach [[John Calipari]] and then for [[Duquesne Dukes men's basketball|Duquesne]], while his mother Mariam for [[Oklahoma City Stars women's basketball|Oklahoma City]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.timesonline.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2022/04/28/adou-thiero-quaker-valley-quakers-division-i-basketball-recruit-kentucky-wildcats-almamy-thiero-mali/65350904007/|newspaper=[[The Beaver County Times]]|title=Adou Thiero's parents came to America to chase a dream. Now he has his own bright future|last=Upadhyaya|date=April 28, 2022|first=Parth}} His mother was selected in the [[2006 WNBA draft]] by the [[Washington Mystics]].{{Cite news|url=https://tribhssn.triblive.com/quaker-valleys-adou-thiero-named-2022-triblive-hssn-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year/|newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Tribune-Review]]|title=Quaker Valley's Adou Thiero named 2022 TribLive HSSN Boys Basketball Player of the Year|date=April 4, 2022|last=Harlan|first=Chris}} Thiero, born in the U.S., spent his early years in Mali with his grandmother, while his parents played college basketball. In 2007, at age three, he returned to the U.S. He attended [[Quaker Valley High School]] in [[Leetsdale, Pennsylvania]], where he played [[basketball]], [[Association football|soccer]] and [[lacrosse]].{{Cite web|url=https://ukathletics.com/sports/mbball/roster/player/adou-thiero/|publisher=[[Kentucky Wildcats]]|title=Adou Thiero|date=August 4, 2022 }} A [[combo guard]], he led Quaker Valley in scoring as a [[sophomore]], averaging 17.7 points per game. Then, as a [[Junior (education year)|junior]] in 2020–21, he remained their leading scorer and averaged 21.8 points as well as a team-leading 5.1 assists, 2.2 steals and 1.2 blocks per game. As a [[Senior (education)|senior]], Thiero averaged 23.3 points, 10.3 rebounds, 5.9 assists, 3.9 steals and 2.3 blocks per game, helping the team compile a record of 27–1 while being undefeated in league play; their only loss came in the [[Pennsylvania Interscholastic Athletic Association]] (PIAA) championship game. He set a school record with 44 points in a game, finished third in school history with 1,624 career points, and received several honors after his senior season including [[Western Pennsylvania Interscholastic Athletic League]] (WPIAL) Player of the Year, ''[[Pittsburgh Tribune-Review|TribLive HSSN]]'' Boys Basketball Player of the Year, and Pennsylvania Class 4A Player of the Year. He committed to playing college basketball for [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], coached by John Calipari, who had coached his father in college.{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3301899/2022/05/09/kentuckys-bet-on-adou-thiero-is-that-hell-embrace-the-challenge-continue-growing/|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|title=Kentucky's bet on Adou Thiero is that he'll embrace the challenge, continue growing|date=May 9, 2022|last=Tucker|first=Kyle}} ==College career== ===Kentucky=== As a [[freshman]] at Kentucky in 2022–23, Thiero appeared in 20 games, averaging 9.5 minutes per game, and recorded averages of 2.3 points and 1.9 rebounds.{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college/pittsburgh/pitt-panthers-likely-missing-adou-thiero|date=May 2, 2024|last=Campbell|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=Pitt Likely Missing Out on Kentucky Transfer|first=Dominic}} He was the team leader in steals in four games and in blocks in three games. In 2023–24, he saw more playing time, appearing in 25 games, 19 as a starter, while missing eight due to injury.{{Cite news|url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article287729835.html|newspaper=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]]|title=After two seasons with Kentucky basketball, Adou Thiero is sticking with John Calipari|date=May 6, 2024|last=Drummond|first=Cameron}} He averaged 7.2 points and five rebounds per game, also totaling 27 blocks which was second on the team.{{Cite web|url=https://arkansas.rivals.com/news/arkansas-makes-final-cut-for-kentucky-transfer-adou-thiero|website=[[Rivals.com]]|title=Arkansas makes final cut for Kentucky transfer Adou Thiero|date=April 19, 2024|last=Choate|first=Mason}} He was Kentucky's leading rebounder in eight games and had five games where he scored double figures; he also posted a [[double-double]] in their game against No. 1 ranked [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], scoring 16 points and 13 rebounds. After the season, Thiero entered his name in the [[2024 NBA draft]] and the [[NCAA transfer portal]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article287236985.html|date=March 30, 2024|last=Roberts|title=Adou Thiero issues statement on future. He could still return to Kentucky basketball team.|work=kentucky.com|first=Ben}} ===Arkansas=== Thiero withdrew from the [[2024 NBA draft]] and transferred to the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]] for the 2024–25 season, following coach Calipari from Kentucky.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/40094868|publisher=[[ESPN]]|title=Ex-Kentucky star Adou Thiero joining John Calipari at Arkansas|date=May 6, 2024 |last1=Borzello|first1=Jeff|last2=Givony|first2=Jonathan |name-list-style=and}} In his lone season at Arkansas, Thiero led the team in scoring, averaging 15.1 points per game. He missed ten games due to an injury, but helped the Razorbacks finish 22–14 overall and make it to the Sweet 16 of the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]]. He declared for the [[2025 NBA draft]] after the season was over. {{cite news |last=Goodson |first=Connor |title=Adou Thiero declares for NBA Draft after one season at Arkansas |url=https://247sports.com/college/arkansas/article/adou-thiero-arkansas-basketball-nba-draft-transfer-portal-return-248032870/ |access-date=July 7, 2025 |work=247 Sports |date=April 8, 2025}} ==Professional career== On June 26, 2025, Thiero was taken in the second round of the [[2025 NBA draft]] by the [[Brooklyn Nets]] with the 36th overall pick. He was then traded to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] for the 45th overall pick, which later became [[Rocco Zikarsky]], and cash considerations as part of a seven-team trade involving [[Kevin Durant]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/los-angeles-lakers-acquire-draft-rights-to-adou-thiero|title=Los Angeles Lakers Acquire Draft Rights to Adou Thiero in Seven-Team Trade|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2025}}{{Cite web |last=Turner |first=Broderick |date=2025-06-27 |title=Lakers trade up again to acquire Adou Thiero at No. 36 in NBA draft |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/lakers-trade-again-select-adou-013055216.html |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}} As the season began, he was recovering from knee surgery{{cite news |last=Klein |first=Ricardo |title=Lakers Make Key Decision on Injured Rookie |url=https://www.si.com/nba/lakers/onsi/news/lakers-make-key-decision-on-injured-rookie |access-date=November 23, 2025 |work=SI.com |date=October 29, 2025}} but on October 29 was sent down to the [[South Bay Lakers]], typically an indication that an injured player is nearing a full recovery. He was recalled by the Lakers on November 2.{{cite news |last=Woike |first=Dan |title=Lakers have recalled forward Adou Thiero |url=https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/news/dan-woike-lakers-recalled-forward-111754446.html |access-date=November 23, 2025 |publisher=Yahoo! Canada |date=November 2, 2025}} He made his NBA debut against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] on November 15, 2025, scoring four points and recording a rebound.{{cite web |title=Los Angeles Lakers vs. Milwaukee Bucks Nov 15, 2025 Box Scores |url=https://www.nba.com/game/lal-vs-mil-0022500231/box-score?watchLive |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 16, 2025}} His first field goal was a dunk during the final minute of the game.{{cite web |title=Giannis Antetokounmpo steps in to assist Lakers after game ball drama|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46984336 |website=ESPN.com |date=November 16, 2025|first=Dave|last=McMenamin|access-date=November 16, 2025}} When teammate [[Jarred Vanderbilt]] attempted to secure the game ball for him after the game ended, officials initially refused to give it to him, insisting that the ball belonged to the Bucks. Eventually, Bucks star [[Giannis Antetokounmpo]] intervened and gave the Lakers the ball.{{Cite web | date= November 16, 2025 | title= Giannis Antetokounmpo helped make sure Adou Thiero got the game ball after debut | website = Silver Screen & Roll | url = https://www.silverscreenandroll.com/lakers-news/100570/adou-thiero-giannis-antetokounmpo-lakers-bucks-nba-debut-game-ball-postgame| access-date = November 17, 2025}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2025}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2025–26 Los Angeles Lakers season|L.A.
